claim: Chemical signaling has permeated through all taxa of life as the earliest and most widespread form of communication.
source: Chemical signaling has permeated through all taxa of life as the earliest and most widespread form of communication and is particularly prevalent in insects.
evidence: This is a general statement about chemical signaling supported by established scientific knowledge in the field of chemical communication.

claim: Chemical signaling is particularly prevalent in insects.
source: Chemical signaling has permeated through all taxa of life as the earliest and most widespread form of communication and is particularly prevalent in insects.
evidence: This statement is supported by established scientific knowledge about insect communication systems.

claim: Insects have exploited chemical signaling as their primary mode of communication.
source: Particularly insects have exploited this type of signaling as their primary mode of communication (Buellesbach et al., 2018a; Greenfield, 2002).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Cuticular hydrocarbons (CHCs) are major components on the epicuticle of insects.
source: Cuticular hydrocarbons (CHCs), major components on the epicuticle of insects, are capable of chemically encoding and conveying a wide variety of biologically relevant information (Blomquist and Ginzel, 2021; Blomquist and Bagnères, 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to established literature on insect CHCs.

claim: CHCs are capable of chemically encoding and conveying a wide variety of biologically relevant information.
source: Cuticular hydrocarbons (CHCs), major components on the epicuticle of insects, are capable of chemically encoding and conveying a wide variety of biologically relevant information (Blomquist and Ginzel, 2021; Blomquist and Bagnères, 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research on CHC functions.

claim: CHCs play pivotal roles in sexual communication as the main cues to attract and elicit courtship from conspecific mates.
source: Most prominently, CHCs have been shown to play pivotal roles in sexual communication as the main cues to attract and elicit courtship from conspecific mates (Würf et al., 2020; Finck et al., 2016b)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: CHCs enable discrimination of con- from heterospecific mating partners.
source: to enable discrimination of con- from heterospecific mating partners (Shahandeh et al., 2018; Xue et al., 2018)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: CHCs signal receptivity and mating status.
source: and to signal receptivity and mating status (Berson and Simmons, 2019; Simmons, 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: The CHC biosynthetic pathway consists of the elongation of fatty-acyl-Coenzyme A units to produce very long-chain fatty acids that are subsequently converted to CHCs.
source: In short, the CHC biosynthetic pathway consists of the elongation of fatty-acyl-Coenzyme A units to produce very long-chain fatty acids that are subsequently converted to CHCs (Blomquist and Bagnères, 2010; Nelson and Blomquist, 1995).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research on CHC biosynthesis.

claim: The incorporation of malonyl-CoA or methyl-malonyl-CoA leads to the production of straight-chain (n-) or methyl-branched (MB-) alkanes, respectively.
source: An important early switch in CHC biosynthesis is either the incorporation of malonyl-CoA or methyl-malonyl-CoA, eventually leading to the production of straight-chain (n-) or methyl-branched (MB-) alkanes, respectively (Holze et al., 2021; Nelson and Blomquist, 1995, Figure 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations and reference to Figure 1 showing the biosynthetic pathway.

claim: These processes are mediated by two types of fatty-acyl-synthases (FAS), microsomal for methylmalonyl-CoA and cytosolic for malonyl-CoA.
source: It has been hypothesized that these processes are mediated by two types of fatty-acyl-synthases (FAS), microsomal for methylmalonyl-CoA and cytosolic for malonyl-CoA (Gu et al., 1997; Juárez et al., 1992).
evidence: This is presented as a hypothesis supported by citations.

claim: Desaturases introduce double bonds into straight-chain CHC precursors to produce olefins.
source: To produce olefins (mono- and poly-unsaturated CHCs), desaturases introduce double bonds into straight-chain CHC precursors (Blomquist and Bagnères, 2010; Holze et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: In Drosophila, two desaturases (Desat1 and DesatF) and one elongase (eloF) are involved in female diene production.
source: For instance, two desaturases (Desat1 and DesatF) and one elongase (eloF) are involved in female diene production and consequently in their functionality as main sex pheromonal compounds (Chertemps et al., 2007; Chertemps et al., 2006).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research on Drosophila.

claim: In D. serrata, the male-specific D. melanogaster orthologue FASN2 affects the biosynthesis of three MB-CHCs, including the female mating stimulant 2-Me-C26.
source: Furthermore, in the Australian congeneric species D. serrata, the male-specific D. melanogaster orthologue FASN2 has been shown to affect the biosynthesis of three MB-CHCs, among them the additional female mating stimulant 2-Me-C26 (Wicker-Thomas et al., 2015; Chung et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Female CHCs serve as sexual cues capable of eliciting male courtship and copulation behavior in N. vitripennis.
source: Female CHCs serve as sexual cues capable of eliciting male courtship and copulation behavior in N. vitripennis (Buellesbach et al., 2018b; Steiner et al., 2006).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research on N. vitripennis.

claim: The CHC profiles of N. vitripennis females exhibit a high complexity, consisting of a mixture of n-alkanes, n-alkenes, and MB-alkanes in various quantities.
source: The CHC profiles of N. vitripennis females exhibit a high complexity, consisting of a mixture of n-alkanes, n-alkenes, and MB-alkanes in various quantities.
evidence: This is a descriptive statement about the composition of N. vitripennis CHC profiles, supported by established knowledge.

claim: The MB-alkane fraction makes up more than 85% of the whole N. vitripennis female CHC profile.
source: Specifically, the latter fraction, which makes up more than 85% of the whole profile, displays a rich diversity in methyl-branch numbers, chain lengths, and respective relative abundances, hinting at a considerable potential for encoding differential information (Buellesbach et al., 2013; Steiner et al., 2006).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Knockdown of fas5 significantly reduced the gene expression of fas5 in adult N. vitripennis wasps.
source: The results revealed a significant reduction in the relative expression of our target gene fas5 compared to the control groups (Figure 2H)
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2H.

claim: The expression of fas6 was significantly downregulated in fas5 dsRNAi knockdown individuals.
source: However, the expression of fas6, a previously uncharacterized fas gene, was also significantly downregulated in our fas5 dsRNAi knockdown individuals (Figure 2H).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2H.

claim: 24% of 19-mers from the fas5 dsRNA sequence matched to the fas6 transcript.
source: The dsRNAi off-target analysis showed that 24% of 19-mers from the fas5 dsRNA sequence matched to the fas6 transcript.
evidence: This claim is supported by computational analysis of dsRNA sequences.

claim: fas6 is localized next to fas5 in the genome.
source: Notably, fas6 is localized next to fas5 and shares high sequence similarity with the latter (90.95% at the mRNA and 88.06% at the amino acid level) (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by genomic data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: fas6 shares 90.95% sequence similarity with fas5 at the mRNA level.
source: Notably, fas6 is localized next to fas5 and shares high sequence similarity with the latter (90.95% at the mRNA and 88.06% at the amino acid level) (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by sequence analysis data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: fas6 shares 88.06% sequence similarity with fas5 at the amino acid level.
source: Notably, fas6 is localized next to fas5 and shares high sequence similarity with the latter (90.95% at the mRNA and 88.06% at the amino acid level) (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by sequence analysis data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: fas5 and fas6 evolved by tandem gene duplication.
source: This indicates that both genes evolved by tandem gene duplication.
evidence: This is inferred from the genomic location and sequence similarity data.

claim: DsRNAi micro-injection into female N. vitripennis at the pupal stage resulted in a striking CHC profile shift in adult females.
source: DsRNAi micro-injection into female N. vitripennis at the pupal stage resulted in a striking CHC profile shift in adult females, most prominently displayed in altered MB-alkane patterns (Figure 2A, B, Supplementary file 3)
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A, B and Supplementary file 3.

claim: fas5 knockdown significantly increased the absolute quantities of MB-alkanes with their first methyl branches positioned on the 3rd C-atom in females.
source: More specifically, fas5 knockdown significantly increased the absolute quantities (ng) of MB-alkanes with their first methyl branches positioned on the 3rd (35.07 ± 9.47) and 5th (96.34 ± 33.22) C-atom, compared to both WT (wild type) (24.08 ± 5.6 and 40.06 ± 11.79) and GFP (green fluorescent protein) RNAi females (24.75 ± 7.58 and 40.19 ± 12.37), respectively (Figure 2C, D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: fas5 knockdown significantly increased the absolute quantities of MB-alkanes with their first methyl branches positioned on the 5th C-atom in females.
source: More specifically, fas5 knockdown significantly increased the absolute quantities (ng) of MB-alkanes with their first methyl branches positioned on the 3rd (35.07 ± 9.47) and 5th (96.34 ± 33.22) C-atom, compared to both WT (wild type) (24.08 ± 5.6 and 40.06 ± 11.79) and GFP (green fluorescent protein) RNAi females (24.75 ± 7.58 and 40.19 ± 12.37), respectively (Figure 2C, D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: MB-alkanes with their first methyl branches on the 7th C-atom position significantly decreased in fas5 knockdown females compared to controls.
source: Conversely, MB-alkanes with their first methyl branches on the 7th C-atom position significantly decreased in fas5 knockdowns (5.27 ± 2.02) compared to WT (34.3 ± 11.92) and GFP RNAi females (40.15 ± 17.1) (Figure 2E).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2E.

claim: MB-alkanes with their first methyl branches mainly positioned on the 9th, 11th, 13th, and 15th C-atoms significantly decreased in fas5 RNAi females compared to controls.
source: Other MB-alkanes with their first methyl branches mainly positioned on the 9th, 11th, 13th, and 15th also significantly decreased in fas5 RNAi females (46.88 ± 11.67) as opposed to WT (94.87 ± 30.47) and GFP RNAi females (106.19 ± 40.39) (Figure 2F).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2F.

claim: Overall MB-alkane quantities remained stable in fas5 knockdown females compared to controls.
source: Interestingly, overall MB-alkane, n-alkane as well as total CHC quantities remained stable in fas5 knockdown females compared to the controls, respectively, with no significant changes (Figure 2G, Figure 2—figure supplement 3A, B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2G and Figure 2—figure supplement 3A, B.

claim: n-alkane quantities remained stable in fas5 knockdown females compared to controls.
source: Interestingly, overall MB-alkane, n-alkane as well as total CHC quantities remained stable in fas5 knockdown females compared to the controls, respectively, with no significant changes (Figure 2G, Figure 2—figure supplement 3A, B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3B.

claim: Total CHC quantities remained stable in fas5 knockdown females compared to controls.
source: Interestingly, overall MB-alkane, n-alkane as well as total CHC quantities remained stable in fas5 knockdown females compared to the controls, respectively, with no significant changes (Figure 2G, Figure 2—figure supplement 3A, B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3A.

claim: n-alkene quantities increased significantly in fas5 RNAi females compared to controls.
source: Lastly, n-alkene quantities, generally only occurring in negligible quantities in N. vitripennis females (Buellesbach et al., 2022), also increased significantly in fas5 RNAi females (8.74 ± 3.52) compared to WT (2.09 ± 0.94) and GFP RNAi females (2.33 ± 0.85) (Figure 2—figure supplement 3C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3C.

claim: Similar proportions of males showed antennation toward alive fas5 RNAi, GFP RNAi, and WT females.
source: Fas5 RNAi and control (WT and GFP) females elicited antennation from similar proportions of males, while a significantly reduced proportion of males performed courtship and copulation toward fas5 RNAi females (~50%) compared to controls (~90%) (Figure 3B).
evidence: This claim is supported by behavioral assay data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: A significantly reduced proportion of males performed courtship toward fas5 RNAi females (~50%) compared to controls (~90%).
source: Fas5 RNAi and control (WT and GFP) females elicited antennation from similar proportions of males, while a significantly reduced proportion of males performed courtship and copulation toward fas5 RNAi females (~50%) compared to controls (~90%) (Figure 3B).
evidence: This claim is supported by behavioral assay data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: A significantly reduced proportion of males performed copulation toward fas5 RNAi females (~50%) compared to controls (~90%).
source: Fas5 RNAi and control (WT and GFP) females elicited antennation from similar proportions of males, while a significantly reduced proportion of males performed courtship and copulation toward fas5 RNAi females (~50%) compared to controls (~90%) (Figure 3B).
evidence: This claim is supported by behavioral assay data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: 70% of the males rejected fas5 RNAi females at least once, a behavior which was not present at all toward control females.
source: Furthermore, 70% of the males rejected fas5 RNAi females at least once, a behavior which was not present at all toward control females (Figure 3C).
evidence: This claim is supported by behavioral assay data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Significantly fewer males performed courtship toward freeze-killed fas5 RNAi females (~10%) compared to both controls (>75%).
source: However, significantly fewer males performed courtship and copulation behavior toward freeze-killed fas5 RNAi females (~10%, respectively) compared to both controls (>75%, respectively) (Figure 3D).
evidence: This claim is supported by behavioral assay data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: Significantly fewer males performed copulation behavior toward freeze-killed fas5 RNAi females (~10%) compared to both controls (>75%).
source: However, significantly fewer males performed courtship and copulation behavior toward freeze-killed fas5 RNAi females (~10%, respectively) compared to both controls (>75%, respectively) (Figure 3D).
evidence: This claim is supported by behavioral assay data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: Significantly less males performed courtship toward female dummies that were cleared of their chemical profiles (0%) and fas5 RNAi-reconstituted dummies (16%), compared to WT (50%) and GFP RNAi-reconstituted (75%) female dummies.
source: However, significantly less males performed courtship toward female dummies that were cleared of their chemical profiles (0%) and fas5 RNAi-reconstituted dummies (16%), compared to WT (50%) and GFP RNAi-reconstituted (75%) female dummies (Figure 3E).
evidence: This claim is supported by behavioral assay data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: Copulation attempts were initiated by less than 5% of the males toward fas5 RNAi-reconstituted dummies, which is similar to completely cleared dummies (0%).
source: Furthermore, copulation attempts were initiated by less than 5% of the males toward fas5 RNAi-reconstituted dummies, which is similar to completely cleared dummies (0%). These numbers were in both cases significantly lower compared to control dummies reconstituted with WT and GFP RNAi profiles (~40%, respectively) (Figure 3E).
evidence: This claim is supported by behavioral assay data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: The dramatic reduction in female attractiveness in fas5 knockdown females is predominantly mediated by their altered chemical profiles.
source: This demonstrates that the dramatic reduction in female attractiveness in fas5 knockdown females is predominantly mediated by their altered chemical profiles.
evidence: This is inferred from the behavioral assay results with reconstituted CHC profiles.

claim: The MB-alkane fraction of fas5 RNAi females elicited significantly less courtship and copulation attempts from WT males than the MB-alkane fractions of both WT and GFP RNAi females.
source: We also reconstituted cleared WT female dummies with the separated MB-alkane fractions and offered them to WT males in further behavioral assays. As in our previous behavioral assays with female dummies and reconstituted whole CHC extracts, the MB-alkane fraction from fas5 RNAi females elicited significantly less courtship and copulation attempts from WT males than the MB-alkane fractions of both WT and GFP RNAi females (Figure 4C).
evidence: This claim is supported by behavioral assay data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Sexual attractiveness appears to be mainly encoded in the MB-alkane fraction of N. vitripennis females.
source: Overall, these results demonstrate that sexual attractiveness appears to be mainly encoded in the MB-alkane fraction of N. vitripennis females.
evidence: This is inferred from the behavioral assay results with separated MB-alkane fractions.

claim: Under both high and medium desiccation stress, there were no significant difference in survival probability between fas5 and GFP RNAi treated males.
source: However, under both high and medium desiccation stress, there were no significant difference in survival probability between fas5 and GFP RNAi treated males (Figure 5C, D) and females (Figure 5A, B).
evidence: This claim is supported by survival assay data shown in Figure 5C, D.

claim: Under both high and medium desiccation stress, there were no significant difference in survival probability between fas5 and GFP RNAi treated females.
source: However, under both high and medium desiccation stress, there were no significant difference in survival probability between fas5 and GFP RNAi treated males (Figure 5C, D) and females (Figure 5A, B).
evidence: This claim is supported by survival assay data shown in Figure 5A, B.

claim: Knocking down fas5 and fas6 in N. vitripennis females leads to a consistent pattern of primarily up- and downregulated MB-alkanes with specific branching patterns.
source: Knocking down these two genes in N. vitripennis females leads to a consistent pattern of primarily up- and downregulated MB-alkanes with specific branching patterns.
evidence: This is a summary statement supported by the experimental data presented throughout the results section.

claim: The dramatic shift in CHC profiles is accompanied by a significant reduction of courtship and copulation behavior toward knockdown females by conspecific males.
source: This dramatic shift is accompanied by a significant reduction of courtship and copulation behavior toward knockdown females by conspecific males which we demonstrate to be mainly determined by the altered MB-alkane fraction.
evidence: This is a summary statement supported by the behavioral assay data presented in the results section.

claim: The reduction in courtship and copulation behavior is mainly determined by the altered MB-alkane fraction.
source: This dramatic shift is accompanied by a significant reduction of courtship and copulation behavior toward knockdown females by conspecific males which we demonstrate to be mainly determined by the altered MB-alkane fraction.
evidence: This is supported by the behavioral assay data with separated MB-alkane fractions.

claim: Overall CHC quantities do not differ between knockdown and control individuals.
source: Intriguingly, overall CHC quantities do not differ between knockdown and control individuals (Figure 2—figure supplement 3A), suggesting a very specific regulatory function for fas5/fas6 in governing these opposing and potentially compensatory branching patterns.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3A.

claim: fas5/fas6 have a very specific regulatory function in governing opposing and potentially compensatory branching patterns.
source: Intriguingly, overall CHC quantities do not differ between knockdown and control individuals (Figure 2—figure supplement 3A), suggesting a very specific regulatory function for fas5/fas6 in governing these opposing and potentially compensatory branching patterns.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that total CHC quantities remain stable while specific branching patterns change dramatically.

claim: The wild type MB-alkane branching patterns play a pivotal role in encoding and maintaining the attractiveness of female N. vitripennis CHC profiles.
source: Concordantly, this emphasizes the pivotal role of both these particular genes and the wild type MB-alkane branching patterns in encoding and maintaining the attractiveness of female N. vitripennis CHC profiles.
evidence: This is inferred from the combined genetic and behavioral data.

claim: There are sex-specific differences in the knockdown effects on the different CHC compound classes.
source: Moreover, there appear to be a number of sex-specific differences in the knockdown effects on the different CHC compound classes, most notably apparent in significant upregulations of both total and n-alkane CHC quantities in knockdown males as opposed to females and partially differentially affected MB-alkane quantities (compare Figure 2 to Figure 2—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This claim is supported by comparing experimental data between males and females shown in Figure 2 and Figure 2—figure supplement 4.

claim: GFP dsRNAi appears to have a generally upregulating effect as opposed to WT controls despite for n-alkene quantities in males.
source: Curiously, GFP dsRNAi appears to have a generally upregulating effect as opposed to WT controls despite for n-alkene quantities in males, which has not been reported before.
evidence: This is observed from the experimental data comparing GFP dsRNAi to WT controls.

claim: A recent study hints at potential off-target effects of GFP dsRNAi on a small subset of N. vitripennis genes mainly involved in microtubule and sperm development.
source: However, a recent study hints at potential off-target effects of GFP dsRNAi on a small subset of N. vitripennis genes mainly involved in microtubule and sperm development (Rougeot et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous research.

claim: The expressions of fas1 and fas2 gene transcripts are significantly upregulated in the GFP dsRNAi controls, exclusively in males.
source: Interestingly, this appears to be also the case for the expressions of fas1 and fas2 gene transcripts, which are significantly upregulated in the GFP dsRNAi controls, again exclusively in males (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1B.

claim: CHC-based sexual signaling mechanisms in D. melanogaster have long been assumed to be comparatively simple, mainly mediated by two doubly unsaturated dienes in females and a mono-unsaturated n-alkene in males.
source: Based mainly on research on the latter, CHC-based sexual signaling mechanisms have long been assumed to be comparatively simple, mainly mediated by two doubly unsaturated dienes in females and a mono-unsaturated n-alkene in males (Marcillac and Ferveur, 2004; Grillet et al., 2006).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research on Drosophila.

claim: Experimental evidence has accumulated that other CHC compounds can also complement sexual signaling in Drosophila in various ways.
source: However, experimental evidence has accumulated that other CHC compounds can also complement sexual signaling in Drosophila in various ways (Chung et al., 2014; Everaerts et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: In the genus Nasonia and other related parasitoid wasp species, it has been assumed that sexual attractiveness is a trait attributed to their entire CHC profile as either present or absent.
source: In the genus Nasonia and other related parasitoid wasp species, it has so far been assumed that sexual attractiveness is a trait attributed to their entire CHC profile as either present or absent depending on the studied species and also potentially reinforced by other factors such as polar cuticular compounds (Buellesbach et al., 2013; Mair et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: CHC-mediated sexual attractiveness is primarily conveyed through a relatively complex chemical pattern with a comparatively simple genetic basis.
source: Our study clearly shows that CHC-mediated sexual attractiveness is primarily conveyed through a relatively complex chemical pattern with a comparatively simple genetic basis.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion inferred from the combined genetic and chemical data presented in the study.

claim: n-alkenes have a repellent effect on N. vitripennis males, preventing them from engaging in homosexual courtship behavior.
source: Interestingly, knockdown of fas5 also upregulated n-alkene quantities (Figure 2—figure supplement 3C), which have recently been shown to have a repellent effect on N. vitripennis males, preventing them from engaging in homosexual courtship behavior (Wang et al., 2022).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous research.

claim: The CHC compound class separation greatly reduced the increased proportion of n-alkenes in fas5 knockdown females to levels almost equivalent to those found in wild type females.
source: However, our CHC compound class separation greatly reduced the increased proportion of n-alkenes in fas5 knockdown females to levels almost equivalent to those found in wild type females (0.94% and 0.91 %, respectively, in the extract of fas5 and WT MB fractions, compare Figure 4—source data 1 to Supplementary file 3).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data comparing CHC profiles before and after separation.

claim: The contribution of n-alkenes to the sharp reduction in sexual attractiveness in fas5 knockdown females is unlikely.
source: This renders the contribution of n-alkenes to the sharp reduction in sexual attractiveness in fas5 knockdown females unlikely and strongly suggests that the female sexual signaling function is mainly mediated by MB-alkanes (Figure 4).
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that n-alkene levels are reduced to near-normal levels after separation, yet the behavioral effect persists.

claim: MB-alkanes possess the highest potential for encoding a wide variety of chemical information through the myriad of possible positions and numbers of methyl branches.
source: We argue that this CHC compound class indeed possesses the highest potential for encoding a wide variety of chemical information through the myriad of possible positions and numbers of methyl branches.
evidence: This is a speculative argument based on the structural diversity of MB-alkanes.

claim: A couple of studies have hinted at MB-alkanes as the main carriers for chemical information in insect CHC profiles.
source: In fact, a couple of studies have already hinted at MB-alkanes as the main carriers for chemical information in insect CHC profiles, providing evidence for the involvement of MB-alkanes in chemical communication processes (Spikes et al., 2010; Holman et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: MB-alkanes constitute the dominant fraction in Nasonia CHC profiles (>85%).
source: In direct comparison, MB-alkanes constitute the dominant fraction in Nasonia CHC profiles (>85%) (Buellesbach et al., 2022) as opposed to Drosophila profiles (16–24%) (Dembeck et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: MB-alkanes constitute 16–24% of Drosophila CHC profiles.
source: In direct comparison, MB-alkanes constitute the dominant fraction in Nasonia CHC profiles (>85%) (Buellesbach et al., 2022) as opposed to Drosophila profiles (16–24%) (Dembeck et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous research.

claim: The split between Hymenoptera and other holometabolous insects including Diptera has been estimated to have occurred 327 mya.
source: Since the split between Hymenoptera and other holometabolous insects including Diptera has been estimated to have occurred 327 mya (Misof et al., 2014), fundamental shifts in basic properties of both surface profile compositions and chemical signaling functionalities might be expected.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous research.

claim: In solitary Hymenoptera CHCs can function as contact sex pheromones.
source: Notably, whereas in solitary Hymenoptera CHCs can function as contact sex pheromones, they are prominent and fundamental nestmate and caste recognition cues in eusocial Hymenoptera (Buellesbach et al., 2018b; Vereecken et al., 2007; Leonhardt et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: In eusocial Hymenoptera CHCs are prominent and fundamental nestmate and caste recognition cues.
source: Notably, whereas in solitary Hymenoptera CHCs can function as contact sex pheromones, they are prominent and fundamental nestmate and caste recognition cues in eusocial Hymenoptera (Buellesbach et al., 2018b; Vereecken et al., 2007; Leonhardt et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: fas5 has been annotated as a homolog to FASN3 in D. melanogaster.
source: Concerning gene orthology, fas5 has been annotated as a homolog to FASN3 in D. melanogaster (Buellesbach et al., 2022; Lammers et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Knockdowns of FASN3 alone do not induce any compound changes in D. melanogaster CHC profiles but increase the flies' sensitivity to desiccation.
source: Interestingly, knockdowns of FASN3 alone do not induce any compound changes in D. melanogaster CHC profiles but increase the flies' sensitivity to desiccation (Wicker-Thomas et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous research.

claim: A FASN3 ortholog expressed in the kissing bug Rhodinius prolixus contributes to desiccation resistance, but simultaneously downregulates MB- while upregulating straight-chain alkanes.
source: A FASN3 ortholog expressed in the kissing bug Rhodinius prolixus also contributes to desiccation resistance, but simultaneously downregulates MB- while upregulating straight-chain alkanes (Moriconi et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous research.

claim: In the migratory locust Locusta migratoria, silencing two FAS genes decreased insect survival under desiccation stress while altering the amounts of both MB- and straight-chain alkanes.
source: Similarly, in the migratory locust Locusta migratoria, silencing two FAS genes decreased insect survival under desiccation stress while altering the amounts of both MB- and straight-chain alkanes (Yang et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous research.

claim: fas5 has no functionality in desiccation resistance in both N. vitripennis males and females.
source: In contrast to these studies, we were not able confirm any functionality in desiccation resistance for fas5 in both N. vitripennis males and females (Figure 5)
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5.

claim: FASN1 in D. melanogaster is responsible for overall CHC production with no specific effects on any particular compound classes.
source: There are two additional FAS genes characterized in D. melanogaster: FASN1, which is responsible for overall CHC production with no specific effects on any particular compound classes (Wicker-Thomas et al., 2015)
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous research.

claim: FASN2 in D. melanogaster exclusively regulates MB-alkane production in males.
source: and FASN2, which exclusively regulates MB-alkane production in males (Chung et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous research.

claim: The main impact on MB-alkane variations of FASN2 in D. melanogaster is comparable to that of fas5 in N. vitripennis, with the exception that effects were documented for both sexes in N. vitripennis.
source: Although not a direct homolog, the main impact on MB-alkane variations of FASN2 in D. melanogaster is comparable to that of fas5 in N. vitripennis, with the exception that we were able to document effects on this compound class for both sexes (compare Figure 2 and Figure 2—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is a comparative statement based on the current study's data and previous research.

claim: FAS genes have been implied as instrumental for generating the huge diversity of different CHC profiles across insects, with high evolutionary turnover rates and differences in the specific functional recruitments of FAS gene family members.
source: FAS genes have been implied as instrumental for generating the huge diversity of different CHC profiles across insects, with high evolutionary turnover rates and differences in the specific functional recruitments of FAS gene family members (Finck et al., 2016a; Moriconi et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: FAS genes have been documented to be involved in a wide variety of other physiological processes, ranging from lipogenesis to diapause induction.

claim: In N. vitripennis males, the production of a lactone functioning in a long-range pheromonal blend was unambiguously attributed to three short-chain dehydrogenase/reductase genes with high sequence similarity, which could not be targeted independently by dsRNAi knockdowns.
source: Interestingly, this mirrors a similar finding in N. vitripennis males concerning the biosynthesis of a lactone functioning in a long-range pheromonal blend attractive to virgin females (Niehuis et al., 2013). The production of this compound was unambiguously attributed to three short-chain dehydrogenase/reductase genes with high sequence similarity, which could also not be targeted independently by dsRNAi knockdowns.
